title: Measles deaths reach 1,323 as dengue toll passes 500
excerpt: Five more children died of measles-like symptoms and five more people of dengue in the 24 hours to 8am on 17 November, DGHS figures show.

image.alt: File photo of the entrance to a paediatric ward at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital
image.credit: File photo: Nahid Hossain / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Five more children died of measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on 17 November, taking the combined measles death toll to 1,323, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Of these, 1,218 are suspected measles deaths and 105 are laboratory-confirmed.

DGHS recorded 1,228 new suspected cases, bringing the total to 250,797, and 86 new confirmed cases, for 25,628 in all. Since 15 March, 224,080 people with suspected measles have been admitted to hospital, and 215,063 have recovered.

Dengue

Dengue killed five more people in the same 24 hours, all in Dhaka division, taking this year's toll to 507. Hospitals admitted 1,537 new patients, and 5,609 were under treatment across the country. The year's total stands at 165,644 cases, with 159,528 recoveries.

Why it matters

Both outbreaks are still active in mid-November. Health NGOs and child-focused organisations running immunisation outreach, community health or WASH programmes may need to keep surge plans in place into December, especially in Dhaka division.

What to watch

  • Whether daily dengue admissions fall as the weather cools.
  • Progress of measles catch-up vaccination in the worst-hit districts.
